About Coinflow

Coinflow is the next-generation payment service provider revolutionizing global financial infrastructure with stablecoins, AI-driven fraud prevention, and instant settlement. Coinflow enables businesses to grow faster with instant settlement, fraud & chargeback indemnity, global pay-ins, multi-currency FX, and unified payouts. Founded in 2023, the company serves marketplaces, fintechs, remittance providers, gaming platforms, and ecommerce merchants worldwide.

Since our seed round in 2024, we’ve achieved 23x revenue growth and scaled to multi-billion-dollar annual transaction volume. In response to this growth, Coinflow announced a $25M Series A in October 2025—led by Pantera Capital, CMT Digital, Coinbase Ventures, Jump Crypto, and Reciprocal Ventures—accelerating our mission to power the world’s fastest-moving businesses with innovative, reliable global payments.

Coinflow is proudly headquartered in Chicago, IL. Learn more at coinflow.cash.

Role Overview

Coinflow is seeking a Head of Engineering to lead our engineering team and take ownership of day-to-day engineering, including prioritization, delivery, technical direction, and team health, that currently runs through the CTO. Coinflow is white-label payments infrastructure: card acquiring, payin/payout across numerous methods, hosted and embedded checkout, and merchant onboarding, operating in a heavily regulated environment where the bar for correctness, security, and reliability is high and non-negotiable.

This is a player-coach role, not a hands-off management job. You'll be in the codebase shipping real work on critical payment paths while building and leading the team. You own the team's deliverables — when something is late, broken, or unclear, it's yours to drive to done.

The first 6-12 months: this role is built around a handoff. Early on, you'll work closely with the CTO and ship alongside the team to earn context and trust. As you prove out judgment and delivery, more of the day-to-day — planning, technical decisions, team ownership — shifts to you. Success looks like the team running confidently under you while the CTO steps back from operational engineering.

Key Responsibilities

In the trenches (player)

  • Write, review, and ship production code on critical payment paths — you stay hands-on

  • Debug the hard stuff: production incidents, reliability gaps, performance and correctness issues

  • Set the technical direction and make the architecture calls that matter

  • Raise the engineering bar through code review, standards, and example

Leading the team (coach)

  • Own delivery — break work down, sequence it, and make sure it lands

  • Mentor every engineer on the team, from senior to junior, leveling people up rather than just directing them

  • Manage and grow the engineers: 1:1s, feedback, performance, hiring, and the occasional hard conversation

  • Own the process — clear requirements before work hits engineering, real ownership per project (DRI), and a feedback loop that catches problems early

  • Be the point of accountability for the team's output to the founders

  • Report to the CTO on personnel matters — performance, team health, and people decisions run through you and surface to the CTO directly

Required Qualifications

  • Senior engineering leader who is still a strong, current IC — able to hold your own in the codebase, not just review it

  • Track record owning delivery for a team: shipping real product, on a real cadence, with real accountability

  • Experience building process without bureaucracy — you know the difference between rigor and overhead

  • Comfortable in our stack: TypeScript/Node (Express, React), MongoDB, ClickHouse, Redis/queues

  • High bar for reliability, security, and correctness — you've operated where mistakes cost money

  • Direct communicator — you write things down and don't hide bad news

Preferred Qualifications

  • Payments experience (acquiring, card networks, ACH, chargebacks, PCI)

  • Stablecoin or blockchain infrastructure experience (Solana programs, EVM smart contracts, on-chain settlement)

  • Experience working in a regulated, compliance-forward environment

  • Early-stage startup experience

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation including base salary, performance bonus, and meaningful ownership

  • Opportunity to own engineering delivery and team leadership at a rapidly scaling fintech company

  • Collaborative and innovative work environment with world-class investors

  • Direct impact on core product and company trajectory during a hyper growth phase

The base salary range for this role is $220,000 - $275,000 USD. The actual base salary offered depends on a variety of factors, including but not limited to experience, education, skills, qualifications and business needs.

In addition, the employee who fills this role will be eligible for an equity grant, allowing you to share in the long-term success of the company. You will also have access to a wide array of benefits, including health and wellness benefits, 401(k) savings plan, and flexible time off.

Join the team rewriting how money moves worldwide—and become a driving force in the $194 trillion cross-border payments market.

We're building the company which will de-risk the largest infrastructure build-out in history.

When people finance GPU clusters, the datacenters housing them, and the infrastructure powering them, they need "offtake" - meaning someone has signed a contract to lease the cluster for a period of time before its even built.

Financing a GPU cluster is inherently risky, since margins are thin and volumes are huge. Lenders don't want to take on the risk that cluster developers can't repay their loan, and cluster developers really don't want to risk not selling their cluster. As a result, risk is offloaded to the customer using fixed-price long-term contracts.

If you don't mitigate this customer risk, there's a bubble. This isn't SaaS anymore - application layer companies sign multi-year contracts for computer and inference, but sell to customers on monthly subscriptions. If you mess up a purchase, it's game over: a minor shift in your revenue growth rate might mean the difference between profit or bankruptcy. But what if companies could exit their contract by selling it back to the market?

Otherwise, as AI scales, compute only becomes available to folks who can effectively take on that risk. A 2-person startup in a San Francisco Victorian can't realistically sign a 5-year take or pay contract on $100m supercomputers. But they may be able to buy the month of liquidity that someone else sold back.

So that's what we make: a liquid market for GPU offtake.

About the role

This is a role for a legal strategist–not a gatekeeper. We're building novel financial infrastructure in a market that doesn't have a rulebook yet. Our General Counsel must be a first-class business partner in the room where deals get shaped, not a checkpoint they pass through at the end.

You'll be the team’s resource for strategic advice and tactical excellence. You need commercial instinct, real strategic judgment, and the maturity to know when to protect the company and when to lean in and get a deal done. We want a thought partner who negotiates contracts that close, balancing our interests with terms our counterparties can actually live with, not just papers that are maximally favorable to SFC.

What you'll own:

  • Set the legal strategy and keep it tightly aligned with where the business is going, not where it's been.

  • Be a strategic thought partner to the founders and deal teams: pressure-test structures, flag the risks that actually matter, and help make the call when the path forward is genuinely ambiguous.

  • Draft, negotiate, and close a wide range of contracts, including offtake agreements, partnerships, vendor deals, and licensing agreements, with a commercial, deal-making mindset that gets to "yes" without giving away the store.

Today, we build trusted, high-quality products that expand access to lending, credit, and savings globally


Our culture


We build trusted products that help people access and discover economic opportunities.


We hold a high bar for quality and craftsmanship. No detail is too small. Trust depends on it.


We’re a global team building products people can actually use, turning complex technology into something simple and reliable.


We stay aligned, move quickly, and think long term, while keeping teams lean and focused on impact.


About the role


We’re looking for a Head of Risk to lead the Risk team and own Aave Labs’ risk-governance framework across its contributions to the Aave Protocol and its products. You’ll coordinate with external risk service providers, set and monitor risk parameters, and provide final internal Risk sign-off on collateral onboarding, material protocol-risk recommendations, and product or strategy launches and material changes. This is a leadership role that requires deep protocol knowledge, strong accountability, and the judgment to make high-stakes decisions.


You’ll lead the Risk team and work closely with embedded quantitative, product and engineering specialists, as well as external risk providers to ensure Aave’s risk posture remains best-in-class as the protocol scales into new markets and asset classes. If you understand market structure, portfolio risk management, and the Aave Protocol at a deep level, and you’re ready to take ownership of risk at scale, this role is designed for you.


How you can make an impact:

  • Lead and build the Risk team, setting direction, priorities, and standards for the function
  • Own and evolve Aave’s risk management frameworks and policies
  • Set minimum review standards and provide independent challenge for product-specific risk frameworks
  • Establish model-risk and data-governance standards for material quantitative models and external risk inputs, including validation, versioning and monitoring
  • Review whether product and engineering controls adequately implement approved risk requirements, with explicit ownership of gaps, exceptions and incident response
  • Establish standards for external risk providers and data dependencies, including methodology, independence, conflicts, data quality, performance and fallback arrangements
  • Own the governance, approval thresholds and escalation process for protocol-risk parameters; oversee monitoring and review material change recommendations
  • Approve and sign off on collateral onboarding decisions and risk assessments
  • Review liquidation performance and recommend improvements to liquidation mechanisms
  • Lead risk governance processes and present risk analyses to the DAO
  • Monitor market structure changes and their implications for protocol risk
  • Take accountability for the quality, independence and timeliness of Risk’s assessments, ensuring residual risks, decision owners and escalation paths are explicit and drive a culture of ownership within the team


Let’s connect if you have:

  • 5+ years of experience in risk management, with a strong preference for DeFi or crypto-native experience
  • Proven experience leading and managing a risk team
  • Deep understanding of the Aave Protocol: its markets, governance, parameters, and risk dynamics
  • Strong grasp of market structure, portfolio risk management, and stress testing methodologies
  • Experience governing risk for composable DeFi products or pooled strategies, including external protocol, liquidity, oracle, counterparty, execution and operational dependencies
  • Experience working with or managing external risk service providers
  • Strong sense of accountability and ownership. You take responsibility for outcomes and hold your team to the same standard
  • Excellent judgment under uncertainty. You’re comfortable making consequential decisions with imperfect information
  • Strong communication skills for governance proposals, risk reports, and stakeholder alignment


Nice to have:

  • Previous experience working directly with DeFi governance processes
  • Background in traditional finance risk management (portfolio, credit, or market risk)
  • Familiarity with risk tooling and simulation platforms used in DeFi


Haven’t quite met all the criteria? Let’s not miss out on the chance to speak. Whilst you might not meet every single requirement, you might bring other, more exciting skills to the companies!

About BIT:

BIT (formerly Matrixport) is a global digital asset financial services and infrastructure group. Headquartered in Singapore and founded in 2019, BIT bridges traditional finance and digital assets through governance-driven financial services and technology.

The firm manages over US$7 billion in assets and facilitates more than US$7 billion in monthly trading volume. BIT offers services including custody, trading, asset and wealth management, liquidity and financing solutions, and tokenised real-world assets (RWA), serving institutional and professional investors globally.

BIT Group entities maintain a licensed and regulated footprint across Singapore, Hong Kong, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States and Bhutan.


For more information, visit www.bit.com


Why Join Us:

At BIT, we tackle complex problems as a team. We encourage openness and promote transparency, respect, and inclusivity. Every team member is valued and has a voice that can be heard. We are always in search of intellectually curious and entrepreneurial individuals who are keen on making an impact in the crypto ecosystem and in building a better product for the next one billion users.


Job Responsibilities:


1. Internal Workflow & Document Administration

  • Initiate and manage all Legal Department requests within the Group's internal management system — including payment applications, contract execution, and document approval workflows.
  • Proactively track the progress of finance approvals, follow up on rejected or pending items, and ensure all workflows are completed.
  • Scan, electronically archive, and register the dispatch and return of all executed original documents — maintaining a complete and auditable document trail at all times.


2. Offshore Entity Records & Corporate Governance

  • Maintain and continuously update a master corporate information register for all entities — covering shareholders, directors, share capital, registered addresses, and key statutory details. Ensure all records are current, accurate, and immediately retrievable.
  • Coordinate with external company secretarial firms to manage the full lifecycle of offshore entities — including new incorporation/registration processes and the dissolution or striking-off of inactive entities. Collect and archive all process documents end-to-end.
  • Act as the internal coordination point for all corporate change requests — including shareholder changes, director appointments and resignations, and share capital adjustments. Issue instructions to external secretarial firms, transmit required documentation, and track all changes through to government system confirmation.
  • Manage the complete electronic filing of all corporate documents arising from incorporation, dissolution, and change processes — including certificates of incorporation, memoranda and articles of association, shareholder registers, board resolutions, and regulatory approvals — filed under a standardised naming convention and folder structure on the Legal Department cloud drive.


3. Global Statutory Compliance & Filing Coordination

  • Identify, track, and manage statutory compliance deadlines across all Group jurisdictions — including Hong Kong, Singapore, BVI, Cayman Islands, Switzerland, and others — covering annual returns, economic substance filings, accounting record maintenance, and other regulatory submissions.
  • Coordinate with internal support departments and external company secretarial firms to collect required internal data ahead of deadlines and ensure external parties submit all filings on time and in good order.
  • Conduct preliminary review of annual service fee invoices and ad-hoc change service invoices received from external secretarial firms and law firms — verify reasonableness and accuracy before initiating payment through the OA system.


4. Internal Stakeholder Support & Information Management

  • Serve as the primary internal point of contact for queries from business units regarding company basic information, group organisational structure charts, and director/shareholder registers.
  • Apply internal information classification and disclosure protocols — provide standard-format materials for routine requests and route complex, sensitive, or non-standard requests to the appropriate Legal team member.
  • Maintain an up-to-date group structure chart and ensure it is accessible to authorised internal stakeholders at all times.


5. Certified True Copies, KYC & Due Diligence Support

  • Prepare certified true copies (CTC), notarised documents, and apostilled documents — including constitutions, certificates of incorporation, and director/shareholder registers — in support of Finance, Business, and Legal team requirements.
  • Compile comprehensive KYC documentation packages for bank account openings, law firm due diligence, and financing due diligence exercises — collecting, organising, and packaging all company qualification documents under standardised naming conventions.
  • Coordinate the urgent courier dispatch of original documents to offshore law firms or company secretarial providers — track logistics end-to-end and confirm receipt to the requesting team.


Job Requirements:


  • Minimum 3–5 years of experience in a Corporate Secretary, company secretarial, or entity management role within a corporate legal department, law firm, or professional services firm.
  • Prior experience managing offshore entities across multiple jurisdictions — particularly BVI, Cayman Islands, Hong Kong, and Singapore — is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience working with external company secretarial firms and law firms across multi-jurisdictional entity portfolios.
  • Background in financial services, fintech, digital assets, or a similarly complex, multi-entity corporate environment is advantageous.
  • Experience supporting KYC documentation preparation, due diligence exercises, or bank account opening processes is a strong plus.
  • Fluency in both written and spoken English and Mandarin Chinese is required — the role involves regular communication with Mandarin-speaking internal stakeholders and external parties across Greater China and Southeast Asia.

Who we are

About Privy

Our mission is to make privacy and user ownership the default online. To do so, we build simple, flexible APIs and tools for developers that make it easy to build new products on crypto rails.

Privy owns the abstractions and infrastructure layer above wallets, integrating across chains, third-party providers, and Stripe products like Treasury and Link. We get to solve hard technical problems while leveraging Stripe's distribution to reach customers like Ramp, Klarna, Deel, Kraken, Hyperliquid, and Fomo — powering experiences for both mainstream users and crypto natives.

Learn more about Privy: Privy and Stripe: Bringing crypto to everyone

About the team

Engineering at Privy is distinguished by:

  • High urgency: Shipping very small iterations, very fast, to learn very quickly.
  • Product taste: Our customers are developers, and to build effective products for them requires technical knowledge - you will often be "the PM".
  • Security mindset: A great portion of our product is trust. While we have a dedicated security team, every engineer brings security to their designs from the start.

In practice, we use boring technology like Node, React, and AWS so we can focus our engineering energy entirely on pushing the boundaries of Privy's core product, e.g. through hardware enclaves, multi-region low latency APIs, and blockchain abstractions that are accessible to mainstream developers.

What you’ll do

As a Security Engineer at Privy, you will help keep a rapidly growing platform secure through hands-on investigation, operational ownership, and building real code to solve real problems. You’ll work across security operations, incident response, application and infrastructure security, and internal tooling.

This is not a role limited to reviewing logs and designs or simply escalating findings. You will carry real ownership for the day-to-day work that protects Privy: investigating anomalies, improving security workflows, and building the automation that makes the team faster and more effective over time. You’ll work closely with engineers across Privy and alongside specialists in cryptography, application security, offensive security, and infrastructure security to turn security expertise into practical, durable outcomes.

Responsibilities

  • Own security engineering work end to end: investigate alerts, findings, anomalies, and security requests; identify root causes; drive remediation; and clearly document outcomes.
  • Participate in Privy’s security on-call rotation, helping respond to incidents, triage alerts, support vulnerability workflows, complete access reviews, and handle security escalations.
  • Build and maintain production-quality tooling that reduces manual work, including alert enrichment, automated triage and routing, remediation workflows, access-review automation, and detection improvements.
  • Lead focused investigations into suspected security events or compromises, gathering evidence methodically and coordinating the appropriate response.
  • Proactively identify recurring sources of operational toil and engineer durable solutions that improve the team’s speed, consistency, and ability to scale.
  • Partner with product and engineering teams to assess security risks, review lower-complexity designs and implementation plans, and make practical security tradeoffs to deliver quickly with quality and soundness.
  • Contribute across Privy’s application, infrastructure, cloud, and product-security surface area, developing broad context while building deeper expertise over time.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • Experience as a security engineer, detection engineer, or similarly hands-on engineer in a technically demanding environment.
  • Strong software-engineering skills in Python, Go, Ruby, or a similar language. You can build maintainable tooling and contribute directly to production fixes, not only one-off scripts.
  • Experience investigating security signals, incidents, vulnerabilities, suspicious activity, or other ambiguous technical problems through to resolution.
  • Familiarity with security operations, incident response, vulnerability management, detection engineering, access reviews, or related operational-security workflows.
  • A strong understanding of web, browser, infrastructure, or cloud security, with the ability to apply that understanding across a broad range of problems.
  • Good judgment under pressure, a methodical approach to investigation, and comfort working independently with agency despite incomplete information.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to explain technical findings, risks, and recommended actions clearly to clients and internal stakeholders alike.
  • A self-directed approach to work: you notice gaps, make progress through ambiguity, and reliably close the loop.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with AWS, GCP, or other cloud-security environments.
  • Experience with detection engineering, security automation, incident-response tooling, or remediation pipelines.
  • Bug-bounty experience, offensive-security exposure, or a strong attacker-minded approach to investigation.
  • Experience with IAM, secrets management, secure production access, or secure CI/CD.
  • Background in application security, infrastructure security, cryptography, or privacy engineering.
  • Experience with fintech, payments, blockchain, or another diligence-forward financial product domain.
  • Experience helping shape security operations, incident-response practices, vulnerability-management workflows, or a bug-bounty program.

BIT Group entities maintain a licensed and regulated footprint across Singapore, Hong Kong, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States and Bhutan.

For more information, visit www.bit.com


Job Responsibilities:

Own the on-chain analytics and transaction monitoring (KYT) product line, including risk scoring methodology, detection rules and thresholds, alert severity tiering, and disposition actions.

Design alert triage and case management workflows, and continuously improve operational metrics such as false positive rate, average time-to-disposition, and alert backlog.

Build a configurable rules engine that enables the Compliance team to self-serve the configuration of monitoring rules and thresholds.

Evaluate and manage third-party on-chain analytics vendors (Chainalysis, Elliptic, TRM, etc.), owning vendor selection, integration, and cost control.

Integrate with adjacent compliance workflows, including sanctions and PEP screening, KYC, withdrawal risk controls, and the Travel Rule.

Ensure a complete audit trail and decision lineage across all dispositions, sufficient to satisfy regulatory inquiries, internal and external audits, and suspicious transaction reporting obligations.


Requirements:

5+ years of compliance product experience in crypto or payments, with end-to-end ownership of a KYT or transaction monitoring product line.

Solid understanding of both the capabilities and the limitations of on-chain analytics — indirect exposure, cross-chain activity, mixing services, and the common sources of false positives.

Demonstrated experience using data and metrics to drive measurable improvements in compliance operations efficiency.

Able to independently produce build-ready PRDs covering rules, state transitions, exception flows, and acceptance criteria.

Working knowledge of FATF Recommendation 16 and Travel Rule requirements, and how they are operationalised within on- and off-ramp flows.

Experience partnering with Compliance, Legal, and Risk functions. Professional working proficiency in both Chinese and English.


Preferred Qualifications:

Hands-on experience implementing the Travel Rule end-to-end in at least one jurisdiction.

Experience with licensing, implementation, or regulatory filings under the Hong Kong SFC, Singapore MAS, or EU MiCA regimes.

Product experience in sanctions screening or name screening, or practical experience applying machine learning to reduce false positives.

Background serving institutional clients or supporting an OTC desk.

Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

The Role

The Autonomous Factory Systems team builds the software that gives Hadrian's factories the ability to sense, decide, and act autonomously. This includes the core robotics stack — perception, behaviors, planning, collision avoidance, and high-level control — alongside orchestration between robots and manufacturing machines and the hardware abstraction layer that connects our software to the machines on the floor.

You will build and manage a team of engineers focused on the robotics side of this stack. This is a people-first management role: your focus is on hiring, growing, and supporting a strong team, while staying close enough to the technical work to help guide direction and staffing decisions.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the people leadership of your engineers: hiring, onboarding, mentorship, career growth, and performance.
  • Build a hiring engine for robotics talent — define the bar, run a strong interview process, and help recruit a top-tier team across perception, planning, behaviors, and control.
  • Ensure engineers are engaged, growing, and set up to do their best work; regularly assess team health and address issues before they become problems.
  • Have real input into technical direction and where we invest headcount, in close partnership with the engineers and technical leads who drive architecture and design.
  • Partner with Hardware, Controls, Product, and Operations to translate business priorities into a sequenced roadmap, and make sure the team is resourced and organized to deliver it.
  • Continuously improve the team's engineering practices and developer lifecycle: planning, design review, code review, testing, simulation, deployment, on-call, and incident response.

What We’re Looking For

  • 5+ years of engineering management experience leading robotics, autonomy, or other complex technical teams in production.
  • A genuine passion for people management — you care about your engineers' growth and happiness as much as you care about what the team ships.
  • A track record of hiring and building strong technical teams, including for hard-to-fill or specialized roles.
  • Technical fluency in robotics concepts (perception, planning, behaviors, control, collision avoidance) to have informed conversations about tradeoffs, evaluate technical leads' proposals, and contribute a useful point of view on direction and prioritization — without needing to be the architect yourself.
  • Strong judgment on organizational design: how to structure a team, allocate headcount across projects, and balance depth vs. breadth as the stack grows.
  • Excellent communication and cross-functional partnership skills — you can align engineers, technical leads, hardware/controls partners, and leadership.
  • A track record of running a healthy team: clear expectations, direct feedback, and a strong sense of ownership among your engineers.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment with high stakes, physical systems, and short iteration cycles.
  • M.S. in Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field.

What Will Set You Apart

  • A track record of scaling a team through a period of fast headcount growth, including building out interview loops and onboarding from scratch.
  • Experience mentoring engineers to grow into broader technical leadership roles.
  • Experience managing engineers across multiple robotics disciplines (e.g., perception and planning)

Compensation

For this role, the target salary range is $249,000 - $299,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

Benefits For Full-time Employees

  • Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees
  • 401k
  • Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need.
  • Flexible vacation policy
  • Equity

ITAR Requirements

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

Use of AI in hiring

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy.

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.


Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page to understand what drives us and how we work.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

The Core Infrastructure – Platforms team is responsible for the foundational platform that powers all Kraken on-premises and cloud infrastructure.

We design and operate the systems that enable all engineering at Kraken; bringing together compute, storage, orchestration, and more into a unified, reliable platform. You’ll join a senior group of engineers working closely with SRE, Networking, and Security to deliver a stable, scalable, and secure foundation for all workloads.

We’re looking for someone to help evolve and scale our Kubernetes platform as a core part of our next-generation infrastructure.

 

The opportunity

  • Gain hands-on experience across Kubernetes cluster operations, deployments, networking, and scalability

  • Help build, and operate Kubernetes clusters across multiple datacenters

  • Triage and organize infrastructure issues, learning our systems and best practices along the way

  • Work with senior engineers to solve complex problems, reducing operational burden from the broader team

  • Build automation and tooling to improve team efficiency and reduce toil

  • Participate in on-call rotation to maintain platform reliability

 
 

What you bring

  • Proven experience of 3+ year of working as a Site Reliability Engineer, Infrastructure/Platform/DevOps Engineer, Software Engineer or similar roles

  • Strong passion for providing technical guidance to stakeholders, with excellent communication skills and a customer-focused approach to resolving Kubernetes-related requests, removing blockers, and enabling engineering teams to succeed

  • Strong understanding of distributed systems fundamentals

  • Strong Linux systems knowledge: comfortable at the shell, understanding processes, networking basics, file systems, permissions

  • Networking fundamentals: TCP/IP, DNS, ports, IP addressing, basic routing, TLS, PKI concepts

  • Understanding of Kubernetes internals (control plane, scheduling, networking, storage) and concepts

  • Familiarity with orchestration or advanced Kubernetes networking (Cilium)

  • Ability to leverage AI tools and agents such as Claude and OpenAI to efficiently deliver business value

  • Scripting or programming experience (Python, Bash, Go, or similar)

 
 

Nice to haves

  • Working experience running Kubernetes clusters

  • Exposure to cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure) or on-premises infrastructure

  • Knowledge of Terraform or other Infrastructure as Code tools

  • Experience with storage systems (e.g., Ceph/Rook)

 
 
 

Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Our commitment

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.

We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.

As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

Financial Institutions – BD & Advisory

  • Build and manage a structured pipeline of target financial institutions — banks, exchanges, clearing houses, asset managers, and market infrastructure providers (e.g CME, ICE/NYSE, DTCC, Nasdaq etc) — tracking each organization across stages of engagement: awareness, evaluation, pilot, and committed.

Working at Wave

  • Our hiring philosophy is rooted in culture and values as much as capability.

  • We generate offers from a transparent formula so your pay is based on your skill and experience, not your ability to negotiate.

  • We have a flexible vacation policy, with most folks taking between 21-30 days off, exclusive of statutory holidays.

  • We offer employees a subsidized health care plan that covers their dependents.

  • We support working parents by offering generous parental leave policies.

  • We care about impact, not optics - work however you work best.

Core Values

  1. We’re egolessly mission driven.

    We never forget why we’re in it—to make life better for everyone that touches our products. The people that use Wave to do their jobs, send money to loved ones or save their day’s wages—they’re our real bosses.

  2. We don’t wait—we live our fullest lives now.

    Collectively, we take care of our users first, but individually we take time offline to live a full life, whether that means choosing our working hours carefully, turning off notifications, or taking long vacations.

  3. We’re embarrassingly honest.

    At most companies, admitting your mistakes is seen as weakness, and direct communication about hard things is taboo. At Wave, being vulnerable and honest about your mistakes is a sign of strength, and giving honest feedback to teammates is an act of generosity.

  4. We maximize our rate of learning.

    We’re always iterating on our personal goals and habits to become more effective and happier. Most importantly, we do this fast. The faster we run these loops—as a company and individuals—the faster we’ll achieve our mission.

Principal Engineer

Build the Future of Global Payments

Veem is transforming how businesses move money around the world. Through modern payment infrastructure, intelligent automation, AI-powered operations, and emerging technologies such as stablecoins and blockchain, we are building faster, simpler, and more scalable global B2B payment experiences.

We are looking for a transformative Principal Engineer to help define the next generation of Veem’s technical architecture and platform strategy.

This is one of the most senior individual-contributor engineering roles at Veem. You will partner closely with executive leadership and teams across Engineering, Product, Data, Security, Compliance, and Operations to lead mission-critical initiatives across payments infrastructure, AI-enabled systems, distributed architecture, and emerging financial technologies.

This is not a maintenance-oriented role. We are looking for a hands-on technical leader who can shape strategy, influence across the organization, mentor senior engineers, and drive meaningful technical transformation.

What You’ll Do

  • Define and drive Veem’s long-term technical architecture across core payments, platform, data, integration, and operational systems.

  • Design scalable, resilient, secure, and highly available distributed systems for global B2B payments.

  • Lead complex, cross-functional engineering initiatives spanning multiple teams and systems.

  • Drive modernization efforts, improve platform scalability, and reduce technical debt.

  • Establish engineering standards for architecture, reliability, observability, security, testing, and operational excellence.

  • Lead AI transformation initiatives across engineering and operations.

  • Design and implement systems using AI agents, LLM workflows, intelligent automation, and AI-assisted developer tooling.

  • Help shape Veem’s strategy around stablecoins, blockchain, digital assets, and modern payment rails.

  • Evaluate emerging technologies, settlement mechanisms, fintech protocols, and platform investments.

  • Mentor senior engineers and technical leaders while raising the engineering bar across the organization.

  • Serve as a trusted technical advisor to executive and engineering leadership.

  • Translate business priorities into scalable, practical, and commercially valuable technical solutions.

What We’re Looking For

  • Approximately 12–18 years of software engineering experience.

  • Proven experience operating at Staff+, Senior Staff, Principal Engineer, Architect, or equivalent level.

  • Deep expertise in distributed systems, backend architecture, APIs, microservices, cloud infrastructure, and event-driven systems.

  • Strong hands-on software engineering and architecture capabilities.

  • Experience leading technically complex initiatives across multiple teams.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence technical strategy without direct authority.

  • Experience in fintech, payments, financial services, or another high-scale, highly regulated technology environment.

  • Strong understanding of scalability, data consistency, reliability, security, fault tolerance, and production operations.

  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain technical trade-offs to executive and non-technical audiences.

  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving, ambiguous, and entrepreneurial environment.

Preferred Experience

  • B2B or cross-border payments.

  • Payment processing, settlement, reconciliation, ledgering, treasury, foreign exchange, or financial APIs.

  • AI agents, LLM integrations, intelligent automation, machine learning platforms, or AI-enabled products.

  • Stablecoins, blockchain infrastructure, digital wallets, crypto payments, or digital assets.

  • Experience at a modern fintech, payments, technology, or AI-native organization.

Technical Environment

  • AWS, GCP, or Azure

  • Distributed and event-driven architectures

  • Modern backend platforms, APIs, and microservices

  • Messaging, streaming, and data systems

  • AI/LLM tooling and agent orchestration frameworks

  • Blockchain, stablecoin, and payment infrastructure

  • Observability, reliability, security, and platform tooling

Why Join Veem?

Shape the Future of Global Payments

You will help define how businesses move money internationally as the industry evolves toward faster, more intelligent, and more flexible payment infrastructure.

Lead High-Impact Technical Transformation

This role provides the scope and influence to drive meaningful change across architecture, engineering practices, platform capabilities, and organizational strategy.

Work on AI, Stablecoins, and Emerging Financial Technology

You will have the opportunity to move beyond theoretical experimentation and help determine how these technologies can be used in real-world financial systems.

Operate With Executive Visibility

You will partner directly with senior leadership and contribute to decisions that shape Veem’s long-term product and technology direction.

Maintain Hands-On Technical Impact

This is a senior leadership role for someone who still wants to engage deeply in architecture, systems, and technical problem-solving.

Join an Entrepreneurial Environment

Veem offers the opportunity to move quickly, challenge assumptions, introduce new ideas, and make a visible impact.

Build Systems That Matter

The systems you help design will support real businesses moving real money across borders. Reliability, speed, trust, and technical quality directly affect our customers.

Mentor and Multiply Engineering Talent

You will have the opportunity to develop senior engineers, strengthen technical leadership, and help shape Veem’s engineering culture.

Meaningful Equity Upside

In addition to competitive compensation, this role includes equity participation and the opportunity to share in the long-term value created as Veem continues to grow.

What Success Looks Like

During your first year, you will be expected to:

  • Build a deep understanding of Veem’s platform, architecture, customers, payment flows, and business strategy.
  • Establish strong relationships with Engineering, Product, Security, Compliance, Data, Operations, and executive leadership.
  • Identify the most important architectural risks, constraints, and opportunities across the platform.
  • Create clear technical direction for several of Veem’s highest-priority initiatives.
  • Lead or materially influence major platform, AI, payment, or modernization programs.
  • Improve the quality and consistency of architecture and technical decision-making across teams.
  • Introduce practical AI capabilities that improve engineering productivity or operational performance.
  • Help define Veem’s technical approach to stablecoins and emerging payment infrastructure.
  • Mentor senior engineers and help strengthen technical leadership across the organization.
  • Deliver measurable improvements in scalability, reliability, developer productivity, or platform capability.
  • Establish yourself as a trusted technical advisor who can bring clarity to Veem’s most complex engineering challenges.

Join Veem

Veem is entering an important stage of its technical evolution.

The future of global payments will be shaped by intelligent automation, real-time infrastructure, new settlement technologies, stronger platform capabilities, and engineering teams that can turn emerging technology into trusted financial products.

As Principal Engineer, you will have the opportunity to help build that future.

You will influence how Veem’s systems are designed, how our engineering organization operates, and how we use AI, stablecoins, blockchain, and modern cloud technologies to create a stronger global payments platform.

If you are a deeply technical, forward-thinking engineering leader who wants to make a company-wide impact, we would love to hear from you.

About us

Velocity is revolutionising the global financial landscape by unifying fiat and digital assets through regulated stablecoin technology. We are tackling some of the most significant inefficiencies in global payments, from the limitations of SWIFT to the cost and delays of cross-border transactions.

Founded by Eric Queathem, with decades of experience scaling and leading payments businesses, Velocity combines deep expertise in regulated financial systems with a fast-growing team across London, Warsaw, New York and Melbourne.

Our platform enables businesses to manage payments, treasury functions, and liquidity in real time, operating 24/7/365. We remove friction in global payouts, cross-border settlements, and treasury operations, seamlessly integrating stablecoin-powered speed with the reliability of traditional finance.

Backed by robust partnerships, including strategic collaborations with Fireblocks and other leading technology providers, we are building trusted infrastructure for scalable global growth.

We recently announced a $38m Series A led by Dragonfly and FirstMark, with participation from QED, Capital One Ventures, Ripple and Coinbase Ventures.

The role

This is a senior, quota-carrying role leading Velocity's sales efforts into the largest and most complex fintech and payments companies across EMEA, working alongside a growing commercial team in London.

You will sell regulated stablecoin payment infrastructure into financial institutions, issuers, acquirers, large PSPs, global marketplaces, and scaled fintechs. Deals are multi-threaded, multi-quarter, and involve treasury, payments, product, risk, and compliance stakeholders on the other side of the table.

Beyond your own number, you will raise the ceiling on how we sell: taking on the accounts that need the most seniority in the room, sharpening pricing and positioning for complex enterprise deals, and working with Velocity's leadership team to shape commercial strategy and prioritisation across the region.

Key responsibilities

  • Own a revenue quota against a portfolio of strategic and enterprise accounts, and be accountable for pipeline generation, progression, and closed business.

  • Source and build your own pipeline through outbound, network, events, and inbound follow-up, with the seniority to open doors at CFO, Treasurer, and Head of Payments level.

  • Own the full sales cycle end to end: prospecting, pitching, discovery, solution shaping, commercial and legal negotiation, close, and go-live, typically spanning several quarters and multiple decision-makers.

  • Structure and negotiate commercially significant agreements, including pricing, liquidity, and settlement terms, in partnership with Finance and Legal.

  • Drive adoption of Velocity across the EMEA payments ecosystem, and build a repeatable, disciplined sales motion with clear qualification, pipeline management, and forecasting.

  • Act as a force multiplier for the wider commercial team, setting the standard on deal strategy and supporting more junior sellers on complex opportunities.

  • Work closely with Product to translate enterprise requirements into product direction, and carry the weight to influence roadmap prioritisation.

  • Represent Velocity at senior level at industry conferences and events across the region.

What we are looking for

  • 6-10+ years' experience in enterprise sales, business development, or partnerships, the majority of it in a quota-carrying closing role.

  • Deep payments, fintech, or financial infrastructure experience, with a sophisticated understanding of how money moves cross-border and where cost, float, and friction sit.

  • A demonstrable track record of consistently hitting or exceeding quota on complex enterprise deals, and the numbers to back it up.

  • Experience closing large, multi-stakeholder deals with financial institutions, PSPs, acquirers, marketplaces, or scaled fintechs, including navigating procurement, risk, and compliance review.

  • A strong, established network across the EMEA payments or fintech ecosystem that you can activate from day one.

  • Experience selling technical or API-based products to business and institutional buyers, with the credibility to hold a conversation with both a treasurer and an engineer.

  • Exposure to stablecoins or digital assets is an advantage, but deep payments experience matters more than prior crypto experience.

Nice to have

Deep experience in one or more of the verticals we sell into:

  • Issuing: issuer-processors, BIN sponsors, and card programme managers, and the funding and settlement mechanics that sit behind a card programme.

  • Acquiring: merchant acquirers, payment facilitators, and ISOs, and where scheme settlement timing, prefunding, and merchant payout cycles tie up working capital.

  • Cross-border and remittance: money transfer operators and remittance providers, correspondent banking relationships, and the cost of holding pre-funded balances across corridors.

  • Banks and EMIs: treasury, liquidity, and nostro management inside a regulated balance sheet.

Why join?

  1. Work on a groundbreaking, forward-thinking solution: Be part of a team leveraging cutting-edge technologies to transform the global financial landscape.

  2. Mission-driven environment with purpose: At Velocity, we prioritize security and user empowerment, ensuring our solutions are built with integrity and designed to make a difference.

  3. Learn from industry leaders: The founding team consists of seasoned operators with a proven track record in the industry, providing invaluable mentorship and guidance as we grow.

  4. Backed by top-tier venture capital: Velocity is supported by premier investors, providing the resources and backing necessary to scale rapidly and execute on our ambitious vision.

  5. Shape the future of global finance: Join an innovative team working on a revolutionary solution that is changing the long-term trajectory of financial operations.

  6. Be part of a company with long-term vision: With a strong regulatory-first approach and a focus on sustainable, scalable growth, Velocity is poised for long-term success.

Benefits

  • Shared ownership: Everyone owns a share of the company. One of our values is to act like an owner, and we back that up with real ownership in the business.

  • Equipment: It is important to have the best tools for the job. We will provide you with a MacBook and will update them regularly. We use all the best modern tools, and if you find an even more efficient way of doing something, we'll adopt it.

  • Health and wellbeing: Paid sick leave, plus medical cover.

  • Pension Contribution

  • Time off: 25 days' holiday plus UK bank holidays.

MoonPay is for builders with something to prove.

This isn't a "work on cool crypto stuff" company. It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. Four offerings make that real: fund, tokenize, trade, and spend. 30M+ customers and 500+ ecosystem partners run on us. Licensed in the U.S. Regulated across the UK, EU, Canada, and Australia.

AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters.

You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together.

About BIT:


BIT (formerly Matrixport) is a global digital asset financial services and infrastructure group. Headquartered in Singapore and founded in 2019, BIT bridges traditional finance and digital assets through governance-driven financial services and technology.


The firm manages over US$7 billion in assets and facilitates more than US$7 billion in monthly trading volume. BIT offers services including custody, trading, asset and wealth management, liquidity and financing solutions, and tokenised real-world assets (RWA), serving institutional and professional investors globally.


BIT Group entities maintain a licensed and regulated footprint across Singapore, Hong Kong, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States and Bhutan.


For more information, visit www.bit.com


Why Join Us:


At BIT, we tackle complex problems as a team. We encourage openness and promote transparency, respect, and inclusivity. Every team member is valued and has a voice that can be heard. We are always in search of intellectually curious and entrepreneurial individuals who are keen on making an impact in the crypto ecosystem and in building a better product for the next one billion users.


About the role:

  • The Group has substantive operations and tax filing obligations across multiple jurisdictions in Asia (including Singapore, Malaysia, Hong Kong, Thailand), Europe, and select offshore/holding jurisdictions. Scope covers corporate income tax, indirect tax (GST/VAT/SST), withholding tax, and transfer pricing.
  • Given the Group's digital asset business, exposure to the tax treatment of crypto/digital asset transactions (e.g. lending/borrowing, custody, trading) is highly relevant and a strong differentiator.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Own tax compliance matters across the Group (tax filings, provisions, tax audits, WHT, GST/indirect tax), ensuring timely and accurate filings across all jurisdictions;
  • Lead the development and maintenance of the Group's tax risk register, tax standards, and related governance documentation, and support their endorsement by senior management;
  • Assess uncertain tax positions for Group financial reporting purposes;
  • Manage transfer pricing matters across the Group, including preparing/reviewing TP documentation (Master File, Local Files), and defending TP policies under audit or review;
  • Analyse withholding tax exposure across cross-border intercompany transactions (financing, licensing, services) spanning multiple jurisdictions;
  • Draft clear, actionable tax positions and guidance for business stakeholders, and lead internal training/education sessions to build tax awareness across Finance and business teams;
  • Liaise directly with internal stakeholders and external advisers (Big 4 and other tax advisers) on technical and compliance matters;
  • Support ad hoc tax input into new business/product set-up, process improvements, and where relevant corporate transactions (e.g. restructuring, IPO readiness).


Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accountancy or related field, with relevant professional accreditation (e.g. ATA by SCTP);
  • 7-10 years of relevant tax experience, with financial services tax experience strongly preferred;
  • Strong technical grounding across direct tax, indirect tax, and transfer pricing, with a demonstrated track record of applying this across multiple jurisdictions and complex group structures;
  • Experience with international transfer pricing (documentation, policy design, defence under audit) in a cross-border, multi-entity environment;
  • Experience building or maintaining tax governance frameworks (tax standards, risk registers, SOPs) is a strong plus;
  • Familiarity with cross-border information reporting regimes (FATCA/CRS/CARF) is a plus;
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate technical tax positions into practical guidance for non-tax stakeholders;
  • Strong analytical skills with keen attention to both detail and the bigger picture;
  • Self-starter, comfortable operating with ambiguity in a fast-paced, start-up-like environment;
  • Able to work independently while also being a collaborative, responsible team player.

We are looking for a Senior Manager of Strategic Finance to join our Finance team at a critical inflection point in the company's growth. About the Company



We believe financial services should be more accessible, that’s why we started Axis. A fully interoperable mobile wallet which enables users to send and receive money from any mobile wallet in Egypt, pay their bills, buy anything online with a virtual Visa card, or scan any QR code to pay for anything in-person. We are expanding beyond payments into investment and wealth experiences that help users save, grow, and manage their financial future through intuitive and trusted digital products.



About the Role



In this role, you will define the voice and language of the Axis experience across our consumer and business products. You'll collaborate closely with Product Managers, Product Designers, Researchers, Marketing, and Customer Experience teams to create intuitive, accessible, and consistent product content that helps users complete tasks with confidence.



Responsibilities



  • Writing clear, concise, and user-centered content for Different Axis products
  • Defining and maintaining Axis's product voice, tone, and content guidelines across all touchpoints
  • Collaborating with Product Designers and Product Managers throughout discovery and delivery to shape intuitive user experiences
  • Using research, usability testing, analytics, and customer feedback to improve product content continuously
  • Simplifying complex financial concepts, regulatory information, and error messages into language users easily understand
  • Building and maintaining a scalable content design system, terminology, and localization guidelines in both Arabic and English
  • Partnering with Marketing, Compliance, Legal, and Customer Experience teams to ensure content is consistent, compliant, and customer-friendly



Qualifications



  • 2+ years of experience in UX Writing, Content Design, Content Strategy, or a similar role
  • Exceptional writing and editing skills in Arabic and English
  • Experience writing for digital products, preferably in fintech, banking, or consumer technology
  • Strong understanding of UX principles, accessibility, information architecture, and content-first design
  • Experience working closely with Product Designers, Product Managers, and User Researchers
  • Experience using Figma and content collaboration tools



Required Skills



  • Experience building content design systems or design language guidelines
  • Experience conducting content testing and usability research
  • Familiarity with localization and multilingual product experiences
  • Proven background in developing content for digital platforms within fintech
  • Understanding of conversational UX, AI-assisted experiences, or chatbot design



Preferred Skills



  • Experience building content design systems or design language guidelines
  • Experience conducting content testing and usability research
  • Familiarity with localization and multilingual product experiences
  • Proven background in developing content for digital platforms within fintech
  • Understanding of conversational UX, AI-assisted experiences, or chatbot design



Pay range and compensation package



Very competitive leave policy, including extended Maternity and Paternity leaves.



Equal Opportunity Statement



We are building with purpose. Our team is driven by outcomes, user impact, and the challenge of building financial tools that serve real people. We value Outcomes over outputs, Data and insight over opinions, Real conversations with users over assumptions, Ownership and accountability, Simplicity in solving complex financial problems. This role reports directly to the Head of Product and plays a key part in our mission to build inclusive financial products.

  • Flexible hybrid working model
  • Medical insurance for you and your family
  • Life insurance coverage

Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

The Role

As Hadrian's first Manager, Early Career Recruiting , you will build and lead our early talent function from the ground up. This is a true 0 to 1 leadership opportunity where you will design the strategy, hire and develop a team, and establish the programs that will bring the next generation of builders into Hadrian. You will create lasting partnerships with top universities, trade schools, and community programs while collaborating closely with engineering and factory operations leaders to scale a best-in-class internship and early career program.

What You’ll Do

  • Build, lead, and grow a team of early career recruiters and program leads, providing coaching, direction, and development
  • Design and execute Hadrian's early career recruiting strategy across universities, trade schools, and community programs for both technical and operational talent
  • Develop and own long-term partnerships with universities, trade schools, student organizations, and career centers
  • Partner with senior leaders and hiring managers across engineering, operations, and manufacturing to define workforce pipeline needs and hiring goals
  • Oversee the full candidate lifecycle ensuring a high-quality, consistent experience from first touch through onboarding
  • Plan and lead campus and trade school recruiting events, information sessions, and brand-building activities
  • Build and maintain proactive talent pipelines for technical and operational roles
  • Define the recruiting metrics and reporting infrastructure to measure program effectiveness and team performance
  • Develop scalable processes, tools, and playbooks that support a growing early career function
  • Serve as a strategic advisor to senior leadership on early career talent trends, market insights, and workforce planning

What We’re Looking For

  • Bachelor's degree and 7+ years of university or early career recruiting experience
  • Proven success building or scaling early career and internship programs in high-growth environments
  • Demonstrated ability to lead, develop, and hold a team accountable to goals and performance
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities across a growing function
  • Experience partnering with diverse stakeholders including technical, operations, and senior leadership teams
  • Seasonal travel for campus and recruiting events
  • Occasional evening or weekend work may be required for events

What Will Set You Apart

The Role

The Autonomous Factory Systems team builds the software that gives Hadrian's factories the ability to sense, decide, and act autonomously. This includes the core robotics stack — perception, behaviors, planning, collision avoidance, and high-level control — alongside orchestration between robots and manufacturing machines and the hardware abstraction layer that connects our software to the machines on the floor.

Perception is central to the future of autonomous systems in the factory. In this role will lead the technical direction of the Autonomous Factory Systems organization’s Perception team. You will be — defining the technical roadmap, shaping the architecture, and driving the work that will meaningfully expand what our robots can sense, understand, and act on. This is a deeply hands-on role for someone who brings sharp technical depth and the experience to drive alignment across teams working at the cutting edge of industrial robotics.

  • Define and drive the multi-year technical roadmap for the Perception Team; align perception capabilities with the broader Autonomous Factory Systems strategy and surface upstream dependencies and risks early
  • Lead architecture of the full perception pipeline — object detection and tracking, semantic and instance segmentation, 6-DoF pose estimation, and scene understanding — designed for the reliability and throughput demands of industrial environments
  • Define the integration surface between perception and adjacent systems (motion planning, manipulation, control, simulation); establish clear, well-documented contracts that downstream teams can build against with confidence
  • Drive sensor fusion strategy across LiDAR, structured light, RGB, and depth cameras; collaborate with hardware teams on sensor selection and calibration pipelines
  • Establish rigorous practices for the team: data collection and labeling pipelines, model training and evaluation workflows, deployment practices, and validation criteria across simulation and real-world environments
  • Raise the technical bar in hiring — define role requirements, conduct technical interviews, and assess candidates with the domain depth the field demands; mentor engineers across levels on perception fundamentals and engineering craft
  • Represent perception in cross-functional design reviews and planning; engage with hardware vendors and research collaborators where relevant
  • Continuously evaluate state-of-the-art research; make deliberate, justified decisions about when and how to incorporate advances into production systems

  • 10+ years of software engineering in computer vision, robotics perception, or autonomous systems, with a track record of technical leadership at Staff or Principal level (or equivalent scope)
  • Expert-level command of 3D computer vision: point cloud processing, depth estimation, stereo and structured light systems, multi-view geometry, and/or LiDAR-based algorithms in production
  • Strong machine learning foundations — model architecture, training infrastructure, and production deployment — with the judgment to know when and how to apply learned approaches versus classical methods
  • Experience in manufacturing, logistics, or other applied robotics environments — familiarity with the reliability and safety constraints that production deployment demands beyond the lab
  • Experience building and deploying real-time perception systems under hard latency and reliability constraints
  • Strong proficiency in C++ and Python; demonstrated ability to write production-quality code and hold a high bar in technical review
  • Proven ability to define architecture across a domain, make and communicate high-stakes technical decisions, and build alignment across teams and organizational boundaries
  • Experience contributing meaningfully to technical hiring — defining role requirements, evaluating candidates, and helping raise team caliber over time

  • M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field with a concentration in computer vision, machine learning, or perception
  • Hands-on experience with sensor fusion techniques including multi-modal calibration, temporal alignment, and uncertainty quantification across sensor modalities

Platform Engineering at Chainalysis provides the shared infrastructure, tooling, and developer experience layer that powers every engineering team. We are moving away from team-owned infrastructure silos and consolidating onto shared, scalable platform patterns. The Foundation discipline owns the substrate: cloud infrastructure, networking, Kubernetes, streaming, and security primitives. Everything else runs on what we build.

We are hiring a Software Engineer II to join the Foundation team. Your job is straightforward: build, improve, and operate the infrastructure primitives that every service at Chainalysis depends on — Kubernetes clusters, cloud networking, streaming infrastructure (Kafka / WarpStream), secrets management, IAM, and the reconcilers that make it all self-service and drift-free. This is an infrastructure-focused IC role at the C4 level, typically suited for someone with 3–5 years of experience. You will work alongside senior engineers who will pair with you, review your work, and invest in your growth. You will report to the Senior Manager of Platform Engineering.

In this role, you'll:

  • Build and maintain cloud infrastructure across AWS and GCP using Terraform — designing the modules and patterns that provision the substrate our services run on, and thinking beyond the immediate use case to how your work is consumed across the organization

  • Operate and evolve multi-tenant Kubernetes clusters (EKS) serving the entire engineering organization — owning node lifecycle, upgrades, security contexts, and networking decisions that affect every team

  • Own the operational side of our streaming infrastructure migration from managed Kafka (MSK) to WarpStream, building and maintaining the tooling that supports it

  • Contribute to platform tooling and reconcilers that underpin our platform contract model — writing Go, working with the Kubernetes API, and building high-quality self-service primitives that engineering teams rely on to declare what their services need

  • Design and maintain foundational networking and security infrastructure — transit gateways, GCP interconnect, ingress, security groups, IAM policies, and IRSA — getting the invisible plumbing right so nobody has to think about it

  • Participate in on-call rotations and drive operational excellence — responding to infrastructure incidents, writing and improving runbooks, and feeding every incident pattern back into automation so the same class of issue never repeats

We're looking for candidates who have:

  • 3+ years of software engineering or infrastructure engineering experience

  • Hands-on experience with AWS services (EC2, EKS, IAM, S3, VPC, or similar) — we're looking for people who have built and operated real infrastructure, not certifications

  • Working knowledge of Kubernetes in production — you have operated or deployed workloads on K8s clusters beyond a local environment

  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform strongly preferred; Pulumi or CloudFormation acceptable)

  • Proficiency in at least one of Go, Python, or shell scripting — Go is preferred because our reconciler work is in Go, but you should be ready to turn your hand to whatever the problem demands

  • Comfort with CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Argo, Jenkins, or similar) and hands-on experience with on-call and incident response — you understand what it means to be accountable for production systems

You might also have:

  • Experience building Kubernetes operators or controllers — CRDs, reconcilers, and the controller-runtime library

  • Familiarity with streaming infrastructure (Kafka, WarpStream, or similar event-driven systems) or depth in networking (VPCs, transit gateways, ingress controllers, DNS, load balancing, and security groups)

  • Experience in regulated environments (SOC 2, ISO-27001, or similar compliance frameworks) or familiarity with GitOps patterns (ArgoCD, Flux)

  • A passion for platform engineering as leverage — you care about making other engineers more productive, and when you see toil, your instinct is to eliminate it

Technologies we use:

  • Languages: Go, Python, Bash/Shell, HCL (Terraform)

  • Cloud: AWS (EC2, EKS, IAM, S3, VPC, Lambda), GCP

  • Infrastructure as Code: Terraform

  • Kubernetes: EKS, Helm, CRDs, controller-runtime

  • Streaming: Kafka, WarpStream (migrating from MSK)

  • Networking: Transit Gateway, GCP Interconnect, Ingress Controllers, DNS, Security Groups

  • Identity & Security: IAM, IRSA, Secrets Management

  • CI/CD: GitHub Actions

  • GitOps: ArgoCD, Flux
